system_overview: This specification models the single-lane bridge problem, a classic concurrency scenario where a bridge over a river is only wide enough to permit a single lane of traffic. Cars travel in two opposing directions along a road that includes the bridge. Cars moving in the same direction may be on the bridge simultaneously, but cars moving in opposite directions must never occupy the bridge at the same time. The problem explores synchronization, mutual exclusion, and fairness in resource sharing.
actors_and_components: The system consists of two groups of cars: one group traveling in one direction (right-to-left) and another traveling in the opposite direction (left-to-right). The road is modeled as a sequence of positions, with a contiguous subset of positions forming the bridge. A waiting queue manages access to the bridge, determining which car enters next when the bridge is available.
state_variables: The system tracks two pieces of state: (1) the current position of each car on the road, represented as a mapping from each car to a position on the road, and (2) an ordered queue of cars waiting to enter the bridge, representing the order in which cars arrived at the bridge entrance.
initial_state: Cars traveling in one direction start at one end of the road, and cars traveling in the opposite direction start at the other end. The waiting queue is initialized with any cars that happen to start adjacent to the bridge entrance.
actions: Three types of movement are possible: (1) Move outside the bridge: a car whose next position is not on the bridge advances one position along the road. If this brings the car to the bridge entrance, it joins the end of the waiting queue. (2) Move inside the bridge: a car already on the bridge advances one position, provided no other car occupies the target position. (3) Enter the bridge: the car at the front of the waiting queue may enter the bridge if either the bridge is empty or all cars currently on the bridge are traveling in the same direction as the entering car and the target position is unoccupied. Cars travel in a circular pattern, returning to their starting position after reaching the far end of the road.
safety_properties: Three safety properties are maintained: (1) No two cars occupy the same bridge position simultaneously. (2) The number of cars on the bridge never exceeds the bridge capacity. (3) Cars traveling in opposite directions are never on the bridge at the same time.
liveness_properties: Two liveness properties hold: (1) Every car that enters the bridge eventually exits the bridge. (2) Every car eventually enters the bridge (no car is permanently denied access).
model_bounds: Four constants define the model: the set of cars traveling in each direction, the set of positions constituting the bridge, and the full set of road positions. For model checking, these must be instantiated with specific finite sets.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for all car movement actions, ensuring every car that can make progress eventually does so. The road is circular: a car reaching one end wraps around to the other end, modeling continuous traffic flow. The bridge must be a strict subset of the road positions, with positions before and after the bridge on each side.
